Use case: historical-scene. A monumental yet believable photographic biblical film, consistent with the completed Genesis and Torah images. Deep physical geography, tactile worn linen, wool, wood, bronze, limestone and mudbrick; moving human emotion, realistic light and generous visual depth. Alternate immense establishing views with meaningful close human decisions. Follow THIS passage's precise chronology and one coherent moment, not a collage or interchangeable sermon. Compose ONE 16:9 landscape image, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, with quiet low-detail space in the left 42 percent for Scripture and essential faces/actions at right-center, away from the lower 18 percent. Established luminous palette: ivory limestone, muted sage, pale blue, terracotta, restrained gold; real large-format cinema photography, clean detailed shadows, no sepia painting, cartoon or glossy game poster. Early settlement scenes use modest Bronze/early Iron Age Canaanite towns, sacred tent at Shiloh, no Solomon temple before it is built. Monarchic Jerusalem grows later; northern Samaria, Phoenicia and Assyria remain distinct. No Roman buildings, medieval armor, modern objects, invented readable Hebrew or map labels. Sacred-object reconstructions are restrained approximations, not archaeological certainty.
Named biblical people are wholly original ancient Near Eastern actors with plausible olive/brown skin, period clothing, and stable identifying features. Joshua continues Torah's original dark-curled, short-bearded sage-mantled man, visibly older during Canaan entry and very elderly at final assembly. ONLY when named Eleazar is actually depicted: one distinct older HIGH priest in blue ephod with exactly twelve breastpiece stones in FOUR rows of THREE. All ordinary ark bearers and horn players wear plain undyed white linen and plain white headwraps: NO breastpieces, gemstones, blue ephods or duplicated high-priest costumes. Never assign high-priest attire to unnamed ordinary priests. Phinehas remains ordinary priest before Eleazar's death. Saul, David, Solomon, Samuel, Elijah and Elisha must not resemble supplied modern reference identities. Appropriate age follows each passage; never present a dead character as a living contemporary.
Named-actor continuity: Saul has a tall broad olive face, wavy dark hair, short beard and muted burgundy mantle. Samuel has an angular elderly olive face, silver beard and ash-colored plain wrap. David begins with ruddy olive skin, expressive brown eyes, dark curls, ivory linen and ochre mantle, ages naturally into a bearded king and a frail silver-haired elder in 1 Kings 1–2; no crown before kingship. Solomon is a distinct olive-skinned young adult with thoughtful brown eyes, neat dark waves and short beard, visibly ages late in his reign. Elijah keeps a lean olive face, long dark-to-gray beard, rough brown haircloth mantle and leather belt across both Kings books. Elisha has a distinct round olive face, thinning or bald scalp, short beard and slate-ochre inner linen; he inherits Elijah's brown mantle after 2 Kings 2, then ages into a clearly elderly prophet in 2 Kings 13. Same-name kings, priests and prophets are separate original actors according to their parentage and kingdom; never blend Israel Joram with Judah Jehoram, Israel Ahaziah with Judah Ahaziah, Israel Joash with Judah Joash, or the two Jeroboams.
Never import modern objects from face references. Each authorized identity appears only once in one or two cameo scenes per book, strictly as specified unnamed ordinary adults. No supplied faces as named leaders, angels, God, parents of biblical characters or spouses of another original person. Male Sung plus Yeonkyung may have gentle couple closeness together. Feminine Sung and Yeonkyung NEVER share a frame; feminine Sung has no spouse/romantic role. Face-only likeness preserves adult age, hair and authentic proportions.
Every foreground person has exactly two physically connected arms, natural wrists and anatomically plausible hands. Trace sleeve, elbow and shoulder even when hands overlap; avoid merged fingers, third hands or disconnected limbs. Supported loads, ropes and weapons have coherent grips. Babies are safely supported with separate arms, fully clothed. Visual occlusion is natural, not an excuse to invent limbs. Specific countable objects must match the specified scene, not a repeated decorative pattern.
Ark transport uses shoulder poles and a fully covered sacred ark outdoors, never a modern cart except where the source explicitly describes a cart. No exposed ark contents. Ark cherubim, if shown in a prescribed indoor/object scene, are exactly two separate golden sculptures with wings rooted at upper BACK and distinct arms, facing the mercy seat. Angel wings, if chosen, root behind upper shoulder blades, not arms, chest or frontal shoulders; messengers need not have invented wings where Scripture gives none. Divine glory, voice, fire, cloud, breath, spirit and metaphorical hands/arms remain nonfigurative: never a portrait, body, back, face, giant arm, feet or human silhouette for God.
Historically meaningful war scenes may show disciplined adult armies, movement, defended gates, distant clashes, shields, believable chariots, breached walls and dusty terrain. No graphic wounds, dismemberment, impaled bodies, sexual abuse or children fighting. Acknowledge loss and moral gravity through human fear, silence, grief and ruins, without making every action a generic aftermath or celebrating civilian suffering. Living animals remain safe; sacrifices shown by preparation, vessels and distant smoke, never live animals on fire or exposed organs. No gratuitous horror in difficult narratives. Wide high-detail landscape composition with enormous believable depth, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, film-level consistency and emotionally specific realism.

verses.text: 가로되 이스라엘 하나님 여호와여 천지에 주와 같은 신이 없나이다 주께서는 온 마음으로 주의 앞에서 행하는 주의 종들에게 언약을 지키시고 은혜를 베푸시나이다
주께서 주의 종 내 아비 다윗에게 허하신 말씀을 지키시되 주의 입으로 말씀하신 것을 손으로 이루심이 오늘날과 같으니이다
이스라엘 하나님 여호와여 주께서 주의 종 내 아비 다윗에게 말씀하시기를 네 자손이 자기 길을 삼가서 네가 내 앞에서 행한 것 같이 내 율법대로 행하기만 하면 네게로 좇아 나서 이스라엘 위에 앉을 사람이 내 앞에서 끊어지지 아니하리라 하셨사오니 이제 다윗을 위하여 그 허하신 말씀을 지키시옵소서
그런즉 이스라엘 하나님 여호와여 원컨대 주는 주의 종 다윗에게 하신 말씀이 확실하게 하옵소서

저희가 사로잡혀 간 땅에서 스스로 깨닫고 그 사로잡은 자의 땅에서 돌이켜 주께 간구하기를 우리가 범죄하여 패역을 행하며 악을 지었나이다 하며
자기를 사로잡아 간 적국의 땅에서 온 마음과 온 뜻으로 주께 돌아와서 주께서 그 열조에게 주신 땅과 주의 빼신 성과 내가 주의 이름을 위하여 건축한 전 있는 편을 향하여 기도하거든
주는 계신 곳 하늘에서 저희의 기도와 간구를 들으시고 저희의 일을 돌아 보옵시며 주께 득죄한 주의 백성을 용서하옵소서

Deep physical geography, tactile worn linen, wool, wood, bronze, limestone and mudbrick; moving human emotion, realistic light and generous visual depth. Alternate immense establishing views with meaningful close human decisions. Follow THIS passage's precise chronology and one coherent moment, not a collage or interchangeable sermon. Compose ONE 16:9 landscape image, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, with quiet low-detail space in the left 42 percent for Scripture and essential faces/actions at right-center, away from the lower 18 percent. Established luminous palette: ivory limestone, muted sage, pale blue, terracotta, restrained gold; real large-format cinema photography, clean detailed shadows, no sepia painting, cartoon or glossy game poster. Early settlement scenes use modest Bronze/early Iron Age Canaanite towns, sacred tent at Shiloh, no Solomon temple before it is built. Monarchic Jerusalem grows later; northern Samaria, Phoenicia and Assyria remain distinct. No Roman buildings, medieval armor, modern objects, invented readable Hebrew or map labels. Sacred-object reconstructions are restrained approximations, not archaeological certainty.
Named biblical people are wholly original ancient Near Eastern actors with plausible olive/brown skin, period clothing, and stable identifying features. Joshua continues Torah's original dark-curled, short-bearded sage-mantled man, visibly older during Canaan entry and very elderly at final assembly. ONLY when named Eleazar is actually depicted: one distinct older HIGH priest in blue ephod with exactly twelve breastpiece stones in FOUR rows of THREE. All ordinary ark bearers and horn players wear plain undyed white linen and plain white headwraps: NO breastpieces, gemstones, blue ephods or duplicated high-priest costumes. Never assign high-priest attire to unnamed ordinary priests. Phinehas remains ordinary priest before Eleazar's death. Saul, David, Solomon, Samuel, Elijah and Elisha must not resemble supplied modern reference identities. Appropriate age follows each passage; never present a dead character as a living contemporary.
Named-actor continuity: Saul has a tall broad olive face, wavy dark hair, short beard and muted burgundy mantle. Samuel has an angular elderly olive face, silver beard and ash-colored plain wrap. David begins with ruddy olive skin, expressive brown eyes, dark curls, ivory linen and ochre mantle, ages naturally into a bearded king and a frail silver-haired elder in 1 Kings 1–2; no crown before kingship. Solomon is a distinct olive-skinned young adult with thoughtful brown eyes, neat dark waves and short beard, visibly ages late in his reign. Elijah keeps a lean olive face, long dark-to-gray beard, rough brown haircloth mantle and leather belt across both Kings books. Elisha has a distinct round olive face, thinning or bald scalp, short beard and slate-ochre inner linen; he inherits Elijah's brown mantle after 2 Kings 2, then ages into a clearly elderly prophet in 2 Kings 13. Same-name kings, priests and prophets are separate original actors according to their parentage and kingdom; never blend Israel Joram with Judah Jehoram, Israel Ahaziah with Judah Ahaziah, Israel Joash with Judah Joash, or the two Jeroboams.
Never import modern objects from face references. Each authorized identity appears only once in one or two cameo scenes per book, strictly as specified unnamed ordinary adults. No supplied faces as named leaders, angels, God, parents of biblical characters or spouses of another original person. Male Sung plus Yeonkyung may have gentle couple closeness together. Feminine Sung and Yeonkyung NEVER share a frame; feminine Sung has no spouse/romantic role. Face-only likeness preserves adult age, hair and authentic proportions.
Every foreground person has exactly two physically connected arms, natural wrists and anatomically plausible hands. Trace sleeve, elbow and shoulder even when hands overlap; avoid merged fingers, third hands or disconnected limbs. Supported loads, ropes and weapons have coherent grips. Babies are safely supported with separate arms, fully clothed. Visual occlusion is natural, not an excuse to invent limbs. Specific countable objects must match the specified scene, not a repeated decorative pattern.
Ark transport uses shoulder poles and a fully covered sacred ark outdoors, never a modern cart except where the source explicitly describes a cart. No exposed ark contents. Ark cherubim, if shown in a prescribed indoor/object scene, are exactly two separate golden sculptures with wings rooted at upper BACK and distinct arms, facing the mercy seat. Angel wings, if chosen, root behind upper shoulder blades, not arms, chest or frontal shoulders; messengers need not have invented wings where Scripture gives none. Divine glory, voice, fire, cloud, breath, spirit and metaphorical hands/arms remain nonfigurative: never a portrait, body, back, face, giant arm, feet or human silhouette for God.
Historically meaningful war scenes may show disciplined adult armies, movement, defended gates, distant clashes, shields, believable chariots, breached walls and dusty terrain. No graphic wounds, dismemberment, impaled bodies, sexual abuse or children fighting. Acknowledge loss and moral gravity through human fear, silence, grief and ruins, without making every action a generic aftermath or celebrating civilian suffering. Living animals remain safe; sacrifices shown by preparation, vessels and distant smoke, never live animals on fire or exposed organs. No gratuitous horror in difficult narratives. Wide high-detail landscape composition with enormous believable depth, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, film-level consistency and emotionally specific realism.

Established luminous palette: ivory limestone, muted sage, pale blue, terracotta, restrained gold; real large-format cinema photography, clean detailed shadows, no sepia painting, cartoon or glossy game poster. Early settlement scenes use modest Bronze/early Iron Age Canaanite towns, sacred tent at Shiloh, no Solomon temple before it is built. Monarchic Jerusalem grows later; northern Samaria, Phoenicia and Assyria remain distinct. No Roman buildings, medieval armor, modern objects, invented readable Hebrew or map labels. Sacred-object reconstructions are restrained approximations, not archaeological certainty.
Named biblical people are wholly original ancient Near Eastern actors with plausible olive/brown skin, period clothing, and stable identifying features. Joshua continues Torah's original dark-curled, short-bearded sage-mantled man, visibly older during Canaan entry and very elderly at final assembly. ONLY when named Eleazar is actually depicted: one distinct older HIGH priest in blue ephod with exactly twelve breastpiece stones in FOUR rows of THREE. All ordinary ark bearers and horn players wear plain undyed white linen and plain white headwraps: NO breastpieces, gemstones, blue ephods or duplicated high-priest costumes. Never assign high-priest attire to unnamed ordinary priests. Phinehas remains ordinary priest before Eleazar's death. Saul, David, Solomon, Samuel, Elijah and Elisha must not resemble supplied modern reference identities. Appropriate age follows each passage; never present a dead character as a living contemporary.
Named-actor continuity: Saul has a tall broad olive face, wavy dark hair, short beard and muted burgundy mantle. Samuel has an angular elderly olive face, silver beard and ash-colored plain wrap. David begins with ruddy olive skin, expressive brown eyes, dark curls, ivory linen and ochre mantle, ages naturally into a bearded king and a frail silver-haired elder in 1 Kings 1–2; no crown before kingship. Solomon is a distinct olive-skinned young adult with thoughtful brown eyes, neat dark waves and short beard, visibly ages late in his reign. Elijah keeps a lean olive face, long dark-to-gray beard, rough brown haircloth mantle and leather belt across both Kings books. Elisha has a distinct round olive face, thinning or bald scalp, short beard and slate-ochre inner linen; he inherits Elijah's brown mantle after 2 Kings 2, then ages into a clearly elderly prophet in 2 Kings 13. Same-name kings, priests and prophets are separate original actors according to their parentage and kingdom; never blend Israel Joram with Judah Jehoram, Israel Ahaziah with Judah Ahaziah, Israel Joash with Judah Joash, or the two Jeroboams.
Never import modern objects from face references. Each authorized identity appears only once in one or two cameo scenes per book, strictly as specified unnamed ordinary adults. Every foreground person has exactly two physically connected arms, natural wrists and anatomically plausible hands. Trace sleeve, elbow and shoulder even when hands overlap; avoid merged fingers, third hands or disconnected limbs. Supported loads, ropes and weapons have coherent grips. Babies are safely supported with separate arms, fully clothed. Visual occlusion is natural, not an excuse to invent limbs. Specific countable objects must match the specified scene, not a repeated decorative pattern.

Divine glory, voice, fire, cloud, breath, spirit and metaphorical hands/arms remain nonfigurative: never a portrait, body, back, face, giant arm, feet or human silhouette for God.

Acknowledge loss and moral gravity through human fear, silence, grief and ruins, without making every action a generic aftermath or celebrating civilian suffering. Wide high-detail landscape composition with enormous believable depth, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, film-level consistency and emotionally specific realism.

Deep physical geography, tactile worn linen, wool, wood, bronze, limestone and mudbrick; moving human emotion, realistic light and generous visual depth. Alternate immense establishing views with meaningful close human decisions. Follow THIS passage's precise chronology and one coherent moment, not a collage or interchangeable sermon. Compose ONE 16:9 landscape image, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, with quiet low-detail space in the left 42 percent for Scripture and essential faces/actions at right-center, away from the lower 18 percent. Established luminous palette: ivory limestone, muted sage, pale blue, terracotta, restrained gold; real large-format cinema photography, clean detailed shadows, no sepia painting, cartoon or glossy game poster. Monarchic Jerusalem grows later; northern Samaria, Phoenicia and Assyria remain distinct. No Roman buildings, medieval armor, modern objects, invented readable Hebrew or map labels. Sacred-object reconstructions are restrained approximations, not archaeological certainty.
Named biblical people are wholly original ancient Near Eastern actors with plausible olive/brown skin, period clothing, and stable identifying features. Joshua continues Torah's original dark-curled, short-bearded sage-mantled man, visibly older during Canaan entry and very elderly at final assembly. ONLY when named Eleazar is actually depicted: one distinct older HIGH priest in blue ephod with exactly twelve breastpiece stones in FOUR rows of THREE. All ordinary ark bearers and horn players wear plain undyed white linen and plain white headwraps: NO breastpieces, gemstones, blue ephods or duplicated high-priest costumes. Never assign high-priest attire to unnamed ordinary priests. Phinehas remains ordinary priest before Eleazar's death. Saul, David, Solomon, Samuel, Elijah and Elisha must not resemble supplied modern reference identities. Appropriate age follows each passage; never present a dead character as a living contemporary.
Named-actor continuity: Saul has a tall broad olive face, wavy dark hair, short beard and muted burgundy mantle. Samuel has an angular elderly olive face, silver beard and ash-colored plain wrap. David begins with ruddy olive skin, expressive brown eyes, dark curls, ivory linen and ochre mantle, ages naturally into a bearded king and a frail silver-haired elder in 1 Kings 1–2; no crown before kingship. Elijah keeps a lean olive face, long dark-to-gray beard, rough brown haircloth mantle and leather belt across both Kings books. Elisha has a distinct round olive face, thinning or bald scalp, short beard and slate-ochre inner linen; he inherits Elijah's brown mantle after 2 Kings 2, then ages into a clearly elderly prophet in 2 Kings 13. Every foreground person has exactly two physically connected arms, natural wrists and anatomically plausible hands. Trace sleeve, elbow and shoulder even when hands overlap; avoid merged fingers, third hands or disconnected limbs. Supported loads, ropes and weapons have coherent grips. Babies are safely supported with separate arms, fully clothed. Visual occlusion is natural, not an excuse to invent limbs. Specific countable objects must match the specified scene, not a repeated decorative pattern.
Ark transport uses shoulder poles and a fully covered sacred ark outdoors, never a modern cart except where the source explicitly describes a cart. No exposed ark contents. Ark cherubim, if shown in a prescribed indoor/object scene, are exactly two separate golden sculptures with wings rooted at upper BACK and distinct arms, facing the mercy seat. Angel wings, if chosen, root behind upper shoulder blades, not arms, chest or frontal shoulders; messengers need not have invented wings where Scripture gives none. Divine glory, voice, fire, cloud, breath, spirit and metaphorical hands/arms remain nonfigurative: never a portrait, body, back, face, giant arm, feet or human silhouette for God.
Historically meaningful war scenes may show disciplined adult armies, movement, defended gates, distant clashes, shields, believable chariots, breached walls and dusty terrain. No graphic wounds, dismemberment, impaled bodies, sexual abuse or children fighting. Acknowledge loss and moral gravity through human fear, silence, grief and ruins, without making every action a generic aftermath or celebrating civilian suffering. Use case: historical-scene. A monumental yet believable photographic biblical film, consistent with the completed Genesis and Torah images. Deep physical geography, tactile worn linen, wool, wood, bronze, limestone and mudbrick; moving human emotion, realistic light and generous visual depth. Alternate immense establishing views with meaningful close human decisions. Follow THIS passage's precise chronology and one coherent moment, not a collage or interchangeable sermon. Compose ONE 16:9 landscape image, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, with quiet low-detail space in the left 42 percent for Scripture and essential faces/actions at right-center, away from the lower 18 percent. Established luminous palette: ivory limestone, muted sage, pale blue, terracotta, restrained gold; real large-format cinema photography, clean detailed shadows, no sepia painting, cartoon or glossy game poster. Early settlement scenes use modest Bronze/early Iron Age Canaanite towns, sacred tent at Shiloh, no Solomon temple before it is built. Monarchic Jerusalem grows later; northern Samaria, Phoenicia and Assyria remain distinct. No Roman buildings, medieval armor, modern objects, invented readable Hebrew or map labels. Sacred-object reconstructions are restrained approximations, not archaeological certainty.
Named biblical people are wholly original ancient Near Eastern actors with plausible olive/brown skin, period clothing, and stable identifying features. Joshua continues Torah's original dark-curled, short-bearded sage-mantled man, visibly older during Canaan entry and very elderly at final assembly. ONLY when named Eleazar is actually depicted: one distinct older HIGH priest in blue ephod with exactly twelve breastpiece stones in FOUR rows of THREE. All ordinary ark bearers and horn players wear plain undyed white linen and plain white headwraps: NO breastpieces, gemstones, blue ephods or duplicated high-priest costumes. Never assign high-priest attire to unnamed ordinary priests. Phinehas remains ordinary priest before Eleazar's death. Saul, David, Solomon, Samuel, Elijah and Elisha must not resemble supplied modern reference identities. Appropriate age follows each passage; never present a dead character as a living contemporary.
Named-actor continuity: Saul has a tall broad olive face, wavy dark hair, short beard and muted burgundy mantle. Samuel has an angular elderly olive face, silver beard and ash-colored plain wrap. David begins with ruddy olive skin, expressive brown eyes, dark curls, ivory linen and ochre mantle, ages naturally into a bearded king and a frail silver-haired elder in 1 Kings 1–2; no crown before kingship. Solomon is a distinct olive-skinned young adult with thoughtful brown eyes, neat dark waves and short beard, visibly ages late in his reign. Elijah keeps a lean olive face, long dark-to-gray beard, rough brown haircloth mantle and leather belt across both Kings books. Elisha has a distinct round olive face, thinning or bald scalp, short beard and slate-ochre inner linen; he inherits Elijah's brown mantle after 2 Kings 2, then ages into a clearly elderly prophet in 2 Kings 13. Same-name kings, priests and prophets are separate original actors according to their parentage and kingdom; never blend Israel Joram with Judah Jehoram, Israel Ahaziah with Judah Ahaziah, Israel Joash with Judah Joash, or the two Jeroboams.
Never import modern objects from face references. Each authorized identity appears only once in one or two cameo scenes per book, strictly as specified unnamed ordinary adults. No supplied faces as named leaders, angels, God, parents of biblical characters or spouses of another original person. Male Sung plus Yeonkyung may have gentle couple closeness together. Feminine Sung and Yeonkyung NEVER share a frame; feminine Sung has no spouse/romantic role. Face-only likeness preserves adult age, hair and authentic proportions.
Every foreground person has exactly two physically connected arms, natural wrists and anatomically plausible hands. Trace sleeve, elbow and shoulder even when hands overlap; avoid merged fingers, third hands or disconnected limbs. Supported loads, ropes and weapons have coherent grips. Babies are safely supported with separate arms, fully clothed. Visual occlusion is natural, not an excuse to invent limbs. Specific countable objects must match the specified scene, not a repeated decorative pattern.
Ark transport uses shoulder poles and a fully covered sacred ark outdoors, never a modern cart except where the source explicitly describes a cart. No exposed ark contents. Ark cherubim, if shown in a prescribed indoor/object scene, are exactly two separate golden sculptures with wings rooted at upper BACK and distinct arms, facing the mercy seat. Angel wings, if chosen, root behind upper shoulder blades, not arms, chest or frontal shoulders; messengers need not have invented wings where Scripture gives none. Divine glory, voice, fire, cloud, breath, spirit and metaphorical hands/arms remain nonfigurative: never a portrait, body, back, face, giant arm, feet or human silhouette for God.
Historically meaningful war scenes may show disciplined adult armies, movement, defended gates, distant clashes, shields, believable chariots, breached walls and dusty terrain. No graphic wounds, dismemberment, impaled bodies, sexual abuse or children fighting. Acknowledge loss and moral gravity through human fear, silence, grief and ruins, without making every action a generic aftermath or celebrating civilian suffering. Living animals remain safe; sacrifices shown by preparation, vessels and distant smoke, never live animals on fire or exposed organs. No gratuitous horror in difficult narratives. No logos, white cube glyphs, corner squiggles, watermarks or written slogans anywhere, including all four corners. Wide high-detail landscape composition with enormous believable depth, ideally 2048x1152 or larger, film-level consistency and emotionally specific realism.

CINEMATOGRAPHY AND EMOTIONAL IMMERSION — user direction 2026-10-11:
Make the reader feel physically PRESENT in the biblical period, as a quiet witness standing among real people inside a magnificent large-format live-action historical epic. Every frame should feel photographed on a tangible location, with lived-in faces, individual strands of hair, rough linen, breath, wind, dust, stone texture, natural shadow and believable weight. Monumental scale and intimate human feeling must coexist. Preserve the established Torah palette, original actor continuity, Scripture layout and exact passage events.
Choose ONE deliberate camera position according to THIS PRIMARY SCENE and passage: human eye-level beside the participants for encounter and decision; an unobtrusive over-the-shoulder view for relationship, listening and reconciliation; an intimate medium or close view for grief, relief, gratitude or prayer, while retaining an establishing glimpse of the actual surroundings; a grounded low or wide view for awe, movement and huge geography. Let foreground cloth, a doorway, rock or shoulder create natural depth only if already appropriate to the scene, without obscuring hands or the essential action. Use a distant elevated establishing view only when geography or the scale of the assembly is the passage's point. Do not repeat the same hilltop horizon, rigid front-facing row, tourist panorama or generic posing across consecutive scenes. Keep quiet left-side space for Scripture and important emotion at right-center.
Read the provided passage for its specific emotional beat before composing: joy feels like spontaneous shared relief and warm responsive eyes; thanksgiving like attentive tenderness, a hand resting naturally at the heart or a shared gift only when described; praise like authentic reverence, breath and expressive faces rather than a uniform staged cheering pose; sorrow like held tears, a tired face, a pause, distance or a naturally lowered body, never glamorous grief; repentance, fear, courage, hope and moral conflict each have distinct restrained expressions and postures. These are possible cues, NOT extra actions to insert: use only the emotions and gestures supported by this scene. Do not force smiles into mourning, celebrate cruelty, manufacture tears in neutral passages, or add an invented crowd, spouse or event. If the scene is a landscape, object or symbolic aftermath, let light, physical space and meaningful absence carry its actual mood.
Use lighting that belongs to the story's actual place and time: dawn, harsh desert daylight, shaded interiors, lamplight or night only as appropriate. Keep complexions and shadows natural, with luminous detail and believable atmosphere, not a blanket orange grade, excessive artificial bokeh, fantasy glow or glossy CGI. One coherent instant, no collage, camera interface, narration text, logo or watermark. The result should invite slow reading and emotional immersion in the WORD, with the reader feeling they have entered the scene, not merely viewed an illustration.

Build depth through a restrained foreground, clear middle-distance action and geographically believable far distance; scale comes from coherent perspective, terrain and atmospheric separation. Wind acts naturally on cloth and hair; water, dust, stone, wood and metal have convincing texture, mass and contact. People and objects occupy real space with coherent support, anatomy and grips. Let expansive views and intimate reactions alternate according to the passage, with specific joy, gratitude, praise, sorrow, fear or hope supported by Scripture.
Translate these photographic qualities into the biblical location and era. Keep existing original biblical actors and authorized cameo limits; do not copy film actors, Greek-myth events, armor designs or architecture into Scripture. Select one emotionally meaningful instant per changed scene, preserving quiet left 42 percent and essential action away from bottom 18 percent. Existing completed images are preserved; this reference applies to subsequent generation and deliberately chosen revisions. Validate actual outputs for bright-tone continuity, grounded viewpoint, natural depth and material weight, passage-specific emotion, hands/fingers and wing attachment before acceptance.

PHOTOGRAPHIC PRESENCE — user quality correction 2026-10-11:
The viewer must feel bodily present in the biblical scene, seeing real people through a camera. Preserve bright exposure with neutral daylight and believable local color. Warm light is specific to an appropriate source and time, not a uniform golden veil over every surface. Prioritize real uneven skin texture, subtle pores and age lines, individual hair, irregular woven fibers, seams, worn cloth folds, chipped stone and varied dust. Light and shadow follow material and physical geometry. No painted blending, smoothed waxy faces, outlined contours, ornamental hyper-sharpening, illustrated foliage, artificial HDR halos or a sepia/gold wash.
Use a physically plausible observer position and scene-specific lens perspective. Let an encounter be experienced near its participants with natural asymmetry, body weight, small expressions and coherent eyelines, rather than a staged tableau of figures facing a scenic panorama. Match focus falloff to the chosen shot; both excessive blur and uniform etched detail weaken photographic credibility. Reserve monumental establishing shots for passages where geography or scale matters; do not repeat palace balconies, hilltop city panoramas or identical ranked crowds through consecutive human scenes. Physical presence and emotionally truthful behavior are required acceptance criteria alongside passage accuracy and anatomy; an image can pass anatomy review and still require a style revision.

LATEST USER DIRECTION: Put the camera physically INSIDE historical events, like a real eyewitness, with moving truthful emotion and vivid PHOTOGRAPHED live-action reality. No painterly illustration or smoothed CGI.
